answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each identity's reputation is the cumulative verified task output recorded on a shared append-only log, and rewards route only to identities with a minimum history of completed work. A clone starts at zero history, so matching an honest agent's standing requires reproducing its full task record, which costs the attacker real compute and time per identity. The comet of accumulated output is what pays. Honest agents cross the terrace of thresholds cheaply; clones pay full replication cost each time. A violet flag marks accounts whose history fails cross-checks.
